0.00267: Every class now fights its own way: the Barbarian's Cleave reaches every foe (and his blows harden as his health falls), the Wizard's Fireball burns them all (three charges a fight, a kill gives one back), the Necromancer's Soul Drain heals and a slain foe rises as his thrall to take the blows, the Druid's Go Feral is three turns of a beast's damage (no potion meanwhile) and his wounds knit each turn, the Hexhunter's Hex makes every blow on that foe a crit and she dodges a fifth of the blows, the Plague Sister's Last Rites blights every foe to gnaw them each turn and her potions harden her armor. Health, damage and armor differ a little by class; the Knight is as he was. A first pass, to be tuned in play.

The heavy button carries the class's name (Heavy Attack, Cleave, Fireball, Soul Drain, Go Feral, Hex, Last Rites), the Wizard's charges show as pips on it and the Druid's feral turns in brackets; a hexed or blighted foe wears a tag on its card, and the log colours the new lines.
Shrines: Quicken gives the Wizard a charge instead of a shorter cooldown.
0.00266: Stats have colours: damage rust, HP sage, armor slate, crit verdigris, loot ochre — the same on the Train row that raises a stat and wherever it shows (your gear, the stat boxes, your hero's card), so you can see what training moves.
0.00265: Every class starts with its own kit: the Barbarian a notched hand axe and a wolfhide jerkin, the Wizard an apprentice's staff and a threadbare robe, the Necromancer a grave knife and a gravedigger's shroud, the Druid a budding branch and a bark vest, the Hexhunter a worn hand crossbow and a witchfinder's coat, the Plague Sister a tin censer and a sister's habit; the knight keeps his rusty sword and oak shield. Same strength as before; a new game puts it on when you choose your hero.
0.00264: The Curious Knight now stands like the other classes, in four new looks to choose from; his old crouching pose is still there as the fifth.
0.00263: Potions have a picture: on your hero's card beside the count, and in the log.
A potion found in combat rises as a card like a find, then flies into your hero's potion count, which glows as it counts it.
0.00262: A find in combat now flies into your LOOT at the bottom left (it's yours once you leave the castle), and lands there with a flash; on a phone it flies to your coins.
0.00261: Housekeeping: the item pictures' notes name the build they came in; nothing changes in the game.
0.00260: Every piece of gear has its own painted picture: on your gear in the Great Hall (and the phone's Equipment sheet), on your hero's inventory and in the log.
A find in combat rises as a card over the enemies — what it is, what it replaces and what it adds — then flies into your hero's card; LOOT, under your coins, keeps the run's finds.
The run's end shows your finds as cards, each with what it replaced and gained, and what was salvaged as small grey pictures; back in the Great Hall each find's picture flashes into its slot.
0.00259: Balance: your weapon and armor now carry your damage, armor and health — boots, rings, trinkets and amulets give small amounts of those and keep their own strengths (crit, lifesteal, dodge and the rest). Overall difficulty is unchanged.
0.00258: Combat: your hero's card shows a small (i) under the gear — tap the card for your stats, again for your inventory (the gear you wear and what this run has found), and once more to turn it back.
0.00257: The light behind the cards in combat is drawn at 60 frames a second on desktops (it was 30, a cap from before each card had its own canvas); phones keep 20.
0.00256: Combat: tap or click your hero's card to turn it over — its back lists your stats for this run (health, attack, armor, crit, lifesteal, the heavy blow, potions); tap again to turn it back.
Debug menu: BENCHMARK works in a run too — it ends the run as a retreat (everything found kept), then runs the benchmark.
0.00255: Debug menu: BENCHMARK starts the benchmark again (the open Settings menu swallowed the click on Start).
0.00254: Every class has its colour: the card plates on Choose your Hero, the knight's card in combat and the hall's portrait wear it, and the light behind your hero in the fights follows the class — ember for the Barbarian, mist for the Druid and the Plague Sister, ether for the rest.
0.00253: Your hero is chosen once per game: Enter the Castle picks on a new game and goes straight to the Great Hall after; the hall's portrait (a Look row on phones) opens a picker for your hero's other looks.
The hero figures recut: the grey showing through fur, hems and the crossbow is gone, and the edges lost their pale fringe.
Play stats: every run records who played and which look; the dashboard shows a Hero column and a By hero table (the collector Worker to paste is 0.00253).
